# Founder-Led Sales Resources {#sec-resources}

Beyond the six core books, these are the resources most worth my time as a founder selling my own product. Grouped by what they're best for.

## Talking to customers honestly

*(Pairs with SPIN + Khalsa.)*

- **The Mom Test — Rob Fitzpatrick.** The single best book on customer conversations. How to ask questions that get you the truth even when everyone is being nice to you. Antidote to the founder's habit of fishing for compliments instead of facts. **Read this first.**

## The founder-led sales canon

- **Founding Sales — Pete Kazanjy** (free at [foundingsales.com](https://www.foundingsales.com)). The definitive handbook for the founder who has to sell before there's a sales team: mindset, process, first hires, tooling. Comprehensive and practical.
- **YC Startup School — "How to Sell" (Tyler Bosmeny, founder of Clever).** ~30-min talk. The founder sales funnel — prospecting → conversion → closing — and why founders are actually *better* first salespeople than pros (passion + product depth). Watch it.
- **Steli Efti / Close blog — "The Startup's Guide to Outbound Sales."** Scrappy, tactical founder-sales content; especially good on follow-up persistence.

## Positioning

*(Upstream of all selling — fix this and every stage gets easier.)*

- **Obviously Awesome — April Dunford.** How to position your product so buyers instantly get why it's for them. If discovery keeps stalling on "I don't get what this is," the problem is positioning, not pitching.

## Problem-centric selling

*(A modern, founder-friendly complement to SPIN + Challenger.)*

- **Gap Selling — Keenan.** Sell the *gap* between the customer's current state and desired future state, quantified. Reinforces "diagnose before you prescribe" with a crisp, current framework. Very compatible with everything above.

## Scaling past founder-led

*(For later — don't over-optimize early.)*

- **Predictable Revenue — Aaron Ross.** The outbound/SDR model ("Cold Calling 2.0") and specialized sales roles. Where to look when you're ready to build a repeatable machine beyond yourself.
- **From Impossible to Inevitable — Aaron Ross & Jason Lemkin**, and **SaaStr (Jason Lemkin)** generally. When and how to make your first sales hires and move from founder-led to a team. Read when you have repeatable, self-sourced revenue — not before.
- **The Sales Acceleration Formula — Mark Roberge (HubSpot).** Building a data-driven, repeatable sales org. Also a "later" book.

## Essays worth bookmarking

- **Paul Graham — "Do Things That Don't Scale."** The philosophical license for founder-led sales: recruiting your first customers by hand is not a hack, it's the job.
- **First Round Review & Lenny's Newsletter** — search "founder-led sales" and "first sales hire." Steady stream of concrete playbooks from operators.

## Suggested reading order

*The Mom Test* → *Obviously Awesome* → *Founding Sales* → then the Bosmeny talk → then *Gap Selling*. Save the "scaling" books for when founder-led sales is already working.
